title: cache-aftermath-quant-bottleneck-diary-oct2025
summary: Notes from a week-long deep-dive into unexpected P95 latency regressions observed after enabling AWQ/GPTQ INT8 kernels for long-context traffic. Hypothesis centers on KV-cache eviction patterns + kernel tiling mismatches producing pathologically inefficient device memory access at burst edges.
body:
Background / motivation:
We landed AWQ/GPTQ INT8 kernels for the 13B family on dedicated nodes (A100-80GB, mixed PCIe/NVLink placement) and saw a systematic increase in tail latency for user sessions with long contexts (>6k tokens) under realistic bursty traffic (websocket chat). P50 unchanged, P95 up ~1.8-2.6x depending on payload. Need to capture why and produce short mitigations and a path to robust kernel selection rules.

Observed symptoms (field):
- P50 stable (~82ms), P95 jumped from ~160ms -> ~420ms on 13B-AWQ INT8 over previous FP16 baseline.
- Increased variance correlated with sequences containing long retrieved history (prefixes frequently longer than cached kv windows).
- Tail events show repeated short spikes inside a single request (multiple internal kernel invocations) rather than single long op.
- No saturation signals on CPU-side dispatcher (GPU utility ~60%).

Experiment environment (controlled repro):
- Node: A100-80GB PCIe (driver 525.60), firmware baseline Oct-2025 image, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN versions pinned.
- Serving binary: runtime-v2.8.1-rc3 with AWQ & GPTQ kernel registry enabled.
- Models: 13B-openvariant (3 variants: FP16 baseline, GPTQ-INT8, AWQ-INT8).
- Workload: replayed production trace (chat sessions) with a burst profile (1000 sessions, 10% long-context >6k tokens, interarrival pareto-k=1.5).
- Metrics captured: kernel timeline traces, nvprof/cupti aggregated counters, per-request breakdown (tokenization, prefix copy, KV cache lookup/hit/miss, kernel launch counts), and device memcpy/sync durations.

Profiling highlights (what we saw):
- Kernel launch rate for AWQ & GPTQ variants increased by ~2.3x vs FP16 per request due to additional per-layer dequant/pack/unpack microkernels.
- KV-cache miss rate rose slightly (from 12% -> 17%) under AWQ in replay — linked to cache invalidation heuristics when quantized KV block sizes changed alignment.
- Host->device memcpy spikes coincide with kernel launch thrashing: observed many small memcpy calls (~8–32KB) instead of a few consolidated transfers.
- L2 cache miss counters on GPU increased for AWQ paths; memory bandwidth utilization spiky rather than smooth, leading to queuing inside SM launch streams.
- Observed tiled GEMM kernels (tile32x128) taking 3–6x longer on some layers for INT8 path; same kernels fine on FP16. Suspected misalignment of vector lanes after packing.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quant packing changes KV block alignment leading to smaller, misaligned device transfers and more frequent memcpy ops -> PCIe overhead and SM starvation for some kernels.
2) AWQ/GPTQ microkernels introduce additional synchronization points (device barriers or inefficient stream usage) that amplify latency under bursts.
3) Kernel choice fallback logic occasionally selects a higher-throughput-but-higher-latency tiling for mid-sequence lengths because of stale profiling hints.
4) Prefetch/warmup heuristics for KV-cache not tuned for smaller packed representations, leading to eviction storms mid-conversation.

Quick repro snippets (notes to copy for debugging):
- Repro config: --model 13B-awq-int8 --seq 6144 --batch 1 --trace kernel,timings,memcpy --replay trace_burst_oct2025.json
- Useful nvprof: nvprof --print-gpu-trace --csv --log-file=nvprof_awq.csv <serve-binary> --trace-config

Micro-observations per-layer:
- Layer 5, 7, 8: large step-up in kernel latency; these are heads with attention dims that result in odd remainder lanes post-packing.
- Output projection kernels (dense) show marginal regressions — likely due to int8->fp32 accumulation inefficiencies.
- KV merge paths: when prefix length crosses 4096 boundary we see a double-copy path (copy into aligned scratch -> pack -> device memcpy) vs single copy in FP16.

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- Coalesced memcpy patch (server-side aggregation of small H2D transfers) -> reduced total memcpy time by ~45% and reduced P95 by ~20% on AWQ. But didn't eliminate pathological kernel slowdowns.
- Force alternative tiling kernel for layers 5-9 (override registry) -> brought per-layer slowouts down, P95 improved to ~1.3x baseline but throughput dropped under sustained load. Tradeoff appears acceptable as a short-term rollout for high-SLO customers.
- Increase KV-cache warm window from 2 to 3 segments -> lowered miss rate back to ~12% but at cost of ~4% additional memory footprint; P95 improved marginally.

Root cause candidate and evidence map:
- Cause: combination of packing-induced misalignment (causes inefficient tiled GEMM) + proliferation of small memcopies creating temporal contention on DMA engines.
- Evidence: correlation between layers with odd alignment and latency spikes, nvprof/delayed memcpy sequences, L2/SM cache counters, and per-layer microkernel duration histograms.

Open questions / unknowns to validate:
- Does AWQ packing layout have a systematic byte-shift that interacts poorly with our kernel packer? Need code walking with a small unit test that verifies packed-row stride alignment.
- Are there device-level DMA queue limits being hit when many small memcopies are in-flight? Need to test with synthetic H2D patterns at equivalent QPS.
- Is kernel selection policy using stale per-node profiles (we currently re-profile weekly) — should we profile on deploy or lazily on first warm requests per model+shape?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Aisha: add micro-unit tests that verify packed-KV alignment for AWQ/GPTQ -> due 2025-10-16 (in progress).
- Marco: implement coalesced memcpy as a runtime toggle and benchmark across FP16/AWQ/GPTQ on A100/H100 -> due 2025-10-18 (PR opened).
- Riley: instrument DMA queue depth counters and run synthetic H2D stress tests to see threshold behaviors -> due 2025-10-17.
- Priya: gate a canary rollout that overrides kernels for suspicious layers for 5% of traffic and monitor SLOs -> due 2025-10-20.

Longer-term proposals (for roadmap):
- Kernel registry: add a 'latency-tail' dimension to kernel scoring so we can prefer slightly lower throughput kernels in latency SLO tiers.
- Packing-aware cache: change KV-cache layout to track packed stride and coalesce H2D at cache-line boundaries. This reduces small transfer counts and reduces eviction churn.
- On-device microkernel rework: collaborate with low-level kernel authors to provide a 'padding-friendly' variant that handles odd lane remainders without falling back to scalar loops.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep raw nvprof dumps and a short script to convert to per-layer histograms. I put the initial dumps in s3://redwood-debug/quant-bust-oct2025/
- This diary is purposely raw — will spin up a more formal root-cause writeup if actions above show reproducible fix path.

Appendix: quick table (experiment snapshots)
- baseline FP16: P50 82ms, P95 160ms, throughput 180 tokens/s per GPU
- GPTQ-INT8 (no mitigations): P50 85ms, P95 420ms, throughput 220 tokens/s per GPU
- AWQ-INT8 (coalesced memcpy): P50 88ms, P95 340ms, throughput 210 tokens/s per GPU
- AWQ-INT8 (override kernels layers 5-9): P50 95ms, P95 210ms, throughput 165 tokens/s per GPU

End diary entry.
